findings.body: The test reads the Google link’s return path, then calls `test-auth/sign-in` and installs its cookie directly. It never follows the app’s Google start and callback flow, so a callback that loses the invite path would still pass. Follow the app flow and substitute only Google’s identity verification.
findings.title: Not done: invite sign-in and onboarding return test

findings.body: The limit test creates circles and admits members sequentially. It can pass if simultaneous joins exceed either the 20-circle or 100-member limit. Exercise overlapping join requests against the real database at both boundaries and assert that only one admission succeeds.
findings.title: Not done: concurrent join limit test

findings.body: After Join, the test checks membership but never checks that exactly one usage event records the member and circle. It also never forces event recording to fail and verifies that the join remains committed with that event uncounted. Those required behaviours could break while this test passes.
findings.title: Not done: join usage event test

findings.body: A failed Join leaves `join.error` set. If the admin then resets the link, a preview refetch can return `INVITE_LINK_INVALID`, but this expression selects the older Join error first. The page shows the generic load error instead of the required invalid-link message. TanStack Query [refetches stale queries on focus](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/important-defaults) and [retains mutation errors until reset](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/reference/interfaces/MutationObserverBaseResult).
findings.title: Show the invalid-link message after an earlier Join error
